title: Drama Queen
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Aliens who saved Earth from a meteor now live in Japan with special privileges. Nomamoto, a runaway factory worker with an abusive alien boss, befriends Kitami, whose family was killed in a crash caused by an alien; Kitami kills an alien and the two dispose of the body, and they set out to kill aliens. Later chapters complicate the story by giving alien characters, such as the twins Lily and Lally, sympathetic backstories.
life_message: Hatred passed from person to person keeps a cycle of pain going, and no one understands a conflict without knowing the whole truth.

content.note: Murder, dismemberment and boiling of a body, and alien-eating described by reviewers; MangaDex tags Gore, MangaUpdates lists Serial Killer and Murderer.
Dark black-humor thriller (MangaUpdates Dark Ambience, Black Humor); a worker burned to death in backstory (animesenpai).
No sexual content noted in sources (MangaDex rates it safe).
Xenophobic insults and an abusive boss likely (to verify); not described in sources.
AniList tags Bullying and (low-ranked) Suicide; MangaUpdates lists Sociopath and Unreliable Narrator (to verify).
Protagonists voice anti-immigrant-style grievances and commit hate crimes (animesenpai); MangaUpdates lists Xenophobia and Racism.
An idol character appears (AniList tag); nothing notable.

dominant: Prejudice and its cycle; revenge; social commentary through black comedy

frames.concerns: Protagonists murder and eat aliens; revenge is the engine and judgment is slow to arrive.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Kitami answers his family's deaths with private revenge killings, not courts (comicbook, animesenpai).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Leads act outside law, which is shown as unequal and covering up alien crimes.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty to dead family and to each other outweighs any civic rule.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Story criticizes aliens' special privileges as unfair rank (comicbook).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern secular Japan; no religious frame noted.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Poverty, factory work and fear for jobs drive Nomamoto's resentment (animesenpai).

folkways.japan: The foreign-resident allegory reflects real Japanese debates on immigration and insider-outsider lines (uchi-soto), described here as context.

delivery.evidence: Publisher tagline says 'hate brings pain'; reviewers call it ambiguous early, later nuanced, not didactic (animesenpai; comicbook).

personified.ideology: Revenge-driven hatred of all aliens after personal loss
Economic-grievance xenophobia (aliens take jobs, act arrogant)
The scapegoated outsider who also faced prejudice

delivery.note: Hatred is embodied by the protagonists themselves rather than lectured against; early reviewers found the aliens' side thin, while later coverage says aliens are humanized (to verify across the run).

winners_losers: Still ongoing; the haters drive the plot but the story increasingly sympathizes with the scapegoated aliens and shows hatred repeating across generations.
